fullPassage:
Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is ①<u>texting</u> on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are ②<u>holding</u> under their desks. Another student seems to be ③<u>working</u> on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to ④<u>listening</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 들을 준비가 된 학생. ready to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①texting: is texting(진행형) 정상. ✅ ②holding: are holding(진행형) 정상. ✅ ③working: seems to be working(진행형) 정상. ❌ ④listening: ready to + V(원형). ready to listen이 맞음.
det.tip: be ready to + V(원형). to부정사 뒤에 동사원형. listening(X) → listen(O).

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by ①<u>creating</u> a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that ②<u>interests</u> you. Even if you are not ③<u>exciting</u> about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be ④<u>useful</u> when it is your time to speak.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주제에 흥미를 느끼지 않더라도. 사람의 감정은 -ed 형용사.
det.analysis: ✅ ①creating: by + V-ing(전치사 + 동명사) 정상. ✅ ②interests: something that interests you 정상. ❌ ③exciting: 주어가 you(사람)이므로 excited가 맞음. exciting은 사물 주어. ✅ ④useful: will be useful(형용사) 정상.
det.tip: excited(흥분한, 사람 감정) vs exciting(흥미진진한, 사물 속성). -ed/-ing 감정형용사 구분.

questions.passage: When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will ①<u>appreciate</u> when others ②<u>comment</u> on your speech. Listening well is ③<u>as</u> important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a ④<u>good</u> listener.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 누구든 더 나은(better) 청자가 될 수 있다. good은 원문과 다름.
det.analysis: ✅ ①appreciate: will appreciate(미래형 동사) 정상. ✅ ②comment: others comment(복수주어+동사원형) 정상. ✅ ③as: as important as(원급비교) 정상. ❌ ④good: 원문은 a better listener. become a better(비교급) 문맥에서 good(원급)은 어법 오류.
det.tip: anyone can become a better listener. better = good의 비교급. 개선을 나타내므로 비교급이 필요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 당신이 발표를 하기를 기다리고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①they: Two students를 받는 대명사 정상. ✅ ②her: Another student(여학생)의 소유격 정상. ✅ ③who: a student who(관계대명사 주격) 정상. ❌ ④giving: wait for + O + to V. waiting for you to give가 맞음.
det.tip: wait for + 목적어 + to V(부정사). giving(X) → to give(O). 5형식 구문.

det.korean: 건설적이고 도움이 되게 하라.
det.analysis: ✅ ④helpful: 원문 'be constructive and helpful'. 건설적인과 병렬. ❌ ①critical(비판적인): constructive와 상충. ❌ ②competitive(경쟁적인): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ③indifferent(무관심한): constructive와 상충.
det.tip: constructive and helpful: 건설적이고 도움이 되는. 병렬 구조에서 긍정적 형용사 짝.

det.tip: listener = 듣는 사람, 청자. 발표 맥락에서 자연스러운 역할.

det.analysis: ✅ ①attitude: 원문 'That is an attitude you will appreciate'. 건설적·도움되는 태도. ❌ ②obstacle(장애물): 감사할 대상이 아님. ❌ ③experiment(실험): 무관. ❌ ④occupation(직업): 무관.
det.tip: attitude = 태도. constructive and helpful한 자세가 감사할 '태도'.

det.tip: supportive look = 지지하는 표정. 유일하게 경청 준비된 학생.

det.tip: Even if = ~하더라도. 관심 없어도 유용한 것을 얻을 수 있다 → 듣지 않아도 된다는 틀림.

det.tip: Fortunately(다행히) ↔ Unfortunately(불행히). 긍정적 내용에 부정 부사 변조.

det.tip: climate: (1)기후 (2)분위기/풍토. communication climate = 소통 분위기.

questions.passage: When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener.

det.korean: 그녀의 건설적인 피드백이 에세이 개선에 도움이 되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ constructive: 소유격 Her + __________ + feedback → 형용사 필요. construct(동사) → constructive(형용사).
det.tip: construct(동사: 건설하다) → constructive(형용사: 건설적인).

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. det.analysis: ✅ That is(주절) + an attitude(보어) + you will appreciate(관계절) + when others comment on your speech(부사절).
det.tip: That is an attitude (that) you will appreciate: 관계대명사 목적격 생략. when절은 시간 부사절.
